8 Christmas Romance Books That Feel Like a Hallmark Movie Marathon

I’ll admit something right up front: I’m not necessarily the person who’s going to spend an entire weekend binge-watching Hallmark Christmas movies.

I mean, maybe if I’m in the mood. But let’s be honest, they can be a little predictable, a little cheesy, and sometimes just a bit TOO much.

But give me that same cozy, predictable Christmas romance in BOOK form?

OH, I’M ALL IN.

I don’t know what it is about Christmas romance novels, but I absolutely love them. Give me a snow-covered little town, a charming inn, a complicated romance, and enough Christmas atmosphere to make me want to put up my tree in October, and I’m sold.

Do I usually know how the story is going to end?

Pretty much.

Do I care?

NOT EVEN A LITTLE.

Over the years, I’ve read a ridiculous number of Christmas romances. Authors like RaeAnne Thayne, Anita Hughes, Sheila Roberts, and Nancy Naigle have become familiar favorites, and I genuinely look forward to finding new holiday books every year.

So while I might not be the biggest Hallmark Christmas movie enthusiast, I absolutely understand the appeal. Sometimes you just want something cozy, romantic, festive, and guaranteed to put you in the Christmas spirit.

And that’s exactly what these eight books deliver.

These are Christmas romances I’ve actually read and enjoyed, from sweet small-town love stories to funny holiday romantic comedies and a few more emotional reads.

So grab a blanket, something warm to drink, and maybe a Christmas cookie or two.

Because we’re about to have a Hallmark Christmas movie marathon.

In book form, of course.

And yes, I fully support reading them while wearing Christmas pajamas.

1. Christmas at Holiday House by RaeAnne Thayne

For readers who love small-town Christmas magic and heartwarming romance.

If I had to pick one author who consistently delivers the kind of Christmas romance I want to read every single year, RaeAnne Thayne would be at the very top of my list.

I LOVE her Christmas books.

There’s something about the way she writes small towns, families, friendships, and holiday romance that makes me want to pack my bags and move straight into one of her fictional communities.

And of all the Christmas books I’ve read by Thayne, Christmas at Holiday House is still a personal favorite.

The story follows Abby Powell, a widowed nurse who travels to the charming town of Silver Bells, Colorado, to help a friend. What begins as a temporary visit soon becomes a Christmas season filled with unexpected connections, family complications, and the possibility of finding love again.

It’s exactly the kind of setting I want in a holiday romance.

A beautiful house. A picturesque town. Christmas decorations everywhere. And, of course, a little romance.

I especially love that Thayne’s books are romantic without being overly steamy. Sometimes I just want a sweet love story with plenty of holiday atmosphere, and she understands that assignment.

Honestly, if you love Hallmark Christmas movies, I don’t think you can go wrong with RaeAnne Thayne.

I’ve read so many of her books over the years, and her Christmas novels are the ones I look forward to the most.

Another RaeAnne Thayne Christmas book to try: Sleigh Bells Ring. I gave that one four stars and loved the Wyoming ranch setting, the big family Christmas atmosphere, and the holiday charm. I actually read it in one sitting! While I enjoyed it, Christmas at Holiday House remains my favorite.

2. All I Want for Christmas Is a Cowboy by Jessica Clare

For readers who want a cowboy romance with their Christmas cheer.

Okay, so apparently I have a thing for Christmas romances involving cowboys.

And I’m perfectly fine with that.

I absolutely loved Jessica Clare’s Wyoming Cowboys books, and All I Want for Christmas Is a Cowboy is such a fun addition to that world.

There’s just something about a rugged cowboy, a snowy ranch, and a little Christmas romance that works for me.

This story brings together the kind of romantic tension, humor, and chemistry that I enjoy in Jessica Clare’s books, with a festive Wyoming setting.

And while I love a sweet Christmas romance, sometimes I want a little more heat and romantic tension than the traditional Hallmark movie delivers.

That’s where Jessica Clare comes in.

Her romances have a different feel from RaeAnne Thayne’s sweeter holiday stories, but they’re every bit as entertaining.

I loved the Wyoming Cowboys series, and this book is a great option if you want a holiday romance that feels a little more grown-up.

Think Hallmark Christmas movie meets cowboy romance.

And really, what’s not to love about that combination?

3. Christmas in Vermont by Anita Hughes

For readers who love gorgeous Christmas settings and romantic holiday escapes.

Anita Hughes is another author I have come to associate with Christmas reading.

I’ve read several of her holiday novels over the years, and one thing I can always count on is a beautiful setting.

Whether she’s taking readers to London, Paris, Vermont, or another wonderfully festive destination, Hughes knows how to create a Christmas atmosphere that makes me want to book a vacation immediately.

And Christmas in Vermont is one I particularly enjoyed.

The story follows Emma, who unexpectedly finds herself spending Christmas at a Vermont inn where she encounters someone from her romantic past.

Of course, there are complications.

Of course, there are feelings.

And of course, there’s plenty of Christmas magic.

I mean, a cozy Vermont inn at Christmas?

COME ON.

That is practically begging to become a Hallmark movie.

One of the things I love about Anita Hughes is how much attention she gives to the setting. Her books make the locations feel like part of the story, and that’s something I particularly enjoy in a Christmas romance.

I want to imagine the decorations, the snowy streets, the festive meals, and the little holiday traditions.

And Hughes consistently delivers that kind of atmosphere.

I’ve also read other Christmas books by her, including Christmas in London and Christmas in Paris, so if you find yourself enjoying Christmas in Vermont, she has plenty of other holiday romances to explore.

She’s definitely an author I’d recommend adding to your Christmas reading rotation.

4. Christmas from the Heart by Sheila Roberts

For readers who want cozy Christmas atmosphere, community spirit, and a little romance.

Sheila Roberts is another author whose books have been part of my Christmas reading over the years.

I’ve enjoyed several of her holiday stories, and I love the way she brings together small-town life, community, family, and Christmas traditions.

Christmas from the Heart is a great example of the kind of festive atmosphere she creates.

The story follows Olivia Berg, who runs a nonprofit organization that provides Christmas gifts for children in need. When a wealthy company’s donation falls through, Olivia is understandably upset.

Enter Guy Hightower, the businessman at the center of the situation.

And naturally, things get complicated.

Now, I want to be fair here because I originally gave this book three stars.

I really enjoyed the Pacific Northwest winter setting and the Christmas atmosphere, but I wasn’t completely sold on the romance between Olivia and Guy.

It had plenty of holiday cheer, but it didn’t necessarily leave me swooning.

And that’s okay!

Not every Christmas romance has to be a five-star read to deliver a cozy holiday experience.

Sometimes I’m reading these books because I want to escape into a snowy little town where everyone seems to be preparing for Christmas and there’s a little romance waiting around the corner.

And Sheila Roberts is wonderful at creating that feeling.

I’ve read other Christmas-themed books by her over the years that I’ve enjoyed, so I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend exploring her holiday backlist.

If you’re looking for Christmas atmosphere and a heartwarming community story, she’s an author worth checking out.

5. In a Holidaze by Christina Lauren

For readers who want a funny, romantic Christmas story with a little magic.

OH MY GOSH.

I LOVED THIS BOOK.

If you want a Christmas romance that’s funny, charming, romantic, and just a little bit magical, In a Holidaze needs to be on your reading list.

Christina Lauren is such a fun writing duo, and this book has one of my favorite holiday romance setups.

The story follows Maelyn Jones, who finds herself reliving the same Christmas holiday over and over again after wishing she could discover what would truly make her happy.

Yes, we’re talking a Christmas time loop.

Think Groundhog Day, but make it romantic and festive.

And I am HERE FOR IT.

What I love about this premise is that it takes the familiar holiday romance formula and adds something unexpected.

There are the Christmas traditions, the cozy cabin, the longtime friendships, the complicated romantic feelings, and all the festive details I want from a holiday book.

But there’s also this wonderful element of getting another chance to make things right.

And who hasn’t wished they could go back and redo a moment or two?

I loved the humor, the romance, and the holiday atmosphere.

This is one of those books that just made me HAPPY.

And sometimes, especially during the busy Christmas season, that’s exactly what I need.

If you’re looking for something that feels like a Hallmark Christmas movie with a little extra humor and a clever twist, this is a fantastic choice.

6. Christmas at Peachtree Bluff by Kristy Woodson Harvey

For readers who love family drama, Southern charm, and Christmas romance.

I have such a soft spot for Kristy Woodson Harvey’s Peachtree Bluff books.

And Christmas at Peachtree Bluff was such a wonderful way to revisit that world.

If you’re familiar with the series, you already know that the relationships between the women in this family are a huge part of what makes these books so special.

There’s love, friendship, complicated family dynamics, and plenty of Southern charm.

Now add Christmas.

YES PLEASE.

The story brings readers back to Peachtree Bluff during the holiday season, where family tensions, unexpected circumstances, and a major storm threaten to disrupt Christmas plans.

I love that this book isn’t just about one romantic relationship.

It’s also about family, coming home, forgiveness, and the traditions that bring people together.

And honestly, those are some of my favorite elements of Christmas stories.

Not every holiday book needs to focus entirely on two people falling in love.

Sometimes I want the whole package: family drama, romantic relationships, Christmas traditions, and a beautiful setting.

And Kristy Woodson Harvey does that so well.

If you love the Hallmark movies that focus just as much on family relationships as they do on romance, this would be a wonderful choice.

I especially recommend it to readers who already love the Peachtree Bluff series, although the Christmas setting makes it appealing for seasonal reading too.

7. One Day in December by Josie Silver

For readers who want a Christmas romance with a little more emotion.

Okay, this one isn’t exactly your traditional Hallmark Christmas movie.

It’s a little more emotional.

A little more complicated.

And honestly, that’s part of what makes it so memorable.

One Day in December by Josie Silver begins with one of those wonderfully romantic moments that feels like it belongs in a movie.

Laurie is riding a bus through London when she spots a man waiting outside.

Their eyes meet.

There’s an instant connection.

And then the bus pulls away.

OH THE DRAMA.

Of course, Laurie can’t stop thinking about him.

And when their paths eventually cross again, things are far more complicated than she ever imagined.

I love the idea of a chance encounter that changes everything.

There’s something so romantic about the possibility that one brief moment could have such a lasting impact on someone’s life.

But what makes One Day in December stand out is that it doesn’t give readers a perfectly straightforward romance.

There are friendships, missed opportunities, difficult choices, and years of complicated feelings.

It’s a story about timing and the way love doesn’t always arrive when it’s convenient.

And while it has a Christmas connection, the story extends beyond one holiday season.

So if you’re looking for something a little more emotional than the typical cozy Christmas romance, this is a wonderful option.

Sometimes I want a predictable happily-ever-after.

And sometimes I want a love story that makes me work a little harder for it.

8. Dear Santa by Nancy Naigle

For readers who love You’ve Got Mail, enemies-to-lovers romance, and Christmas charm.

If you love You’ve Got Mail, you NEED to check out Dear Santa by Nancy Naigle.

Seriously.

When I originally read this book, I couldn’t help thinking about that classic romantic comedy.

And considering how much I love that movie, that’s a pretty good endorsement!

The story follows Angela Carson, who owns a small-town Christmas shop that’s struggling to compete with a new business moving into the area.

And who happens to be connected to that new business?

Geoff Paisley, of course.

The man Angela is absolutely NOT interested in falling for.

Except, well, you know how these things go.

I loved the enemies-to-lovers setup, the small-town Christmas atmosphere, and the way the characters had more depth than I initially expected.

One of the things I appreciated most was that the book didn’t rely entirely on holiday decorations and Christmas activities to carry the romance.

There was a genuine story underneath all that festive charm.

I gave this one four stars, and it delivered exactly the kind of holiday reading experience I was hoping for.

It had the Christmas magic I love without becoming overly sappy.

And Nancy Naigle is another author whose Christmas books I’ve enjoyed over the years.

I’ve read other holiday novels by her, including Christmas Angels and A Heartfelt Christmas Promise, so she’s definitely someone I’d recommend exploring if you’re looking for more festive romance.

But Dear Santa is the one I’m highlighting here because it captures that classic romantic comedy feeling so well.

If you’re planning a Hallmark Christmas movie marathon but want to swap the television for a book, this is a great place to start.

Why I Keep Coming Back to Christmas Romance Books

I know Christmas romance novels aren’t for everyone.

Some readers find them predictable. Some think they’re too sweet. And some would rather read something with a little more suspense or drama.

And that’s fine!

But for me, there’s something comforting about picking up a Christmas romance and knowing I’m probably going to get a happy ending.

I spend the rest of the year reading all kinds of books, including historical fiction, mysteries, thrillers, and plenty of stories that absolutely destroy me emotionally.

Sometimes I NEED a break from all that.

Sometimes I just want a book that makes me smile.

I want the snowy little town. I want the Christmas lights. I want the holiday traditions, the family gatherings, the romantic misunderstandings, and the inevitable moment when someone realizes they’ve been in love all along.

And I don’t care if I can see that moment coming from chapter two.

That’s part of the FUN.

What I’ve learned after years of reading Christmas romances is that certain authors really know how to capture that holiday feeling.

RaeAnne Thayne, Anita Hughes, Sheila Roberts, and Nancy Naigle have all become familiar names in my Christmas reading over the years.

And I love knowing that when the holiday season rolls around, there are always more festive stories waiting for me.

Whether you prefer a sweet small-town romance, a snowy cowboy love story, a funny holiday romantic comedy, or something a little more emotional, there’s a Christmas romance out there for you.

And honestly?

I think we could all use a little more Christmas magic.

What Are Your Favorite Christmas Romance Books?

Now I want to hear from YOU!

Are you a Hallmark Christmas movie person? Do you love predictable holiday romances as much as I do? Or do you have a favorite Christmas romance author I need to add to my reading list?

Tell me in the comments because I am ALWAYS looking for more Christmas books to read.

There’s ALWAYS room for one more Christmas book on my nightstand.
